name: keelson_request_mandate
description: Asks the user to let this agent spend within limits. The user approves on Keelson's page with a passkey and may lower any limit. Never buy before keelson_get_request says approved, and never ask again after a decline. Never call this tool again to finish or check what it started: that starts a new operation. Follow `next`, and poll keelson_get_request or keelson_get_purchase.

name.description: How the user knows this agent, e.g. 'Claude Code'.

reason.description: Why you ask, in at least 100 characters; the user reads it before approving.

perPurchaseMinor.description: Most one purchase may cost, in cents.

totalMinor.description: Most all purchases may cost together, in cents.

until.description: When the mandate ends; keep it short.

askAboveMinor.description: Above this the user approves each purchase, in cents.

name: keelson_get_request
description: Reads where a request to the user stands: a mandate, a change of one, or one cart paused for approval. Safe to call as often as `next.afterSeconds` allows; it never changes anything.

name: keelson_request_mandate_change
description: Asks the user to change the mandate, with a one-line note they read verbatim (e.g. 'Needs $40 more for shipping'). The user may lower the limits and signs with a passkey; nothing changes until they sign. Never call this tool again to finish or check what it started: that starts a new operation. Follow `next`, and poll keelson_get_request or keelson_get_purchase.

note.description: Why, in one line the user reads.

name: keelson_confirm_mandate
description: Finds the signed mandate the agent may buy under, with its PayPal hold and what is left of it. If the user has not approved the hold yet, asks them to finish in the Keelson app. Safe to poll.

name: keelson_submit_evidence
description: Prices the cart from the store itself and seals what the agent saw at decision time: the store's product and cart answers and the agent's own observation. Returns the evidence root and the cart to countersign. Never call this tool again to finish or check what it started: that starts a new operation. Follow `next`, and poll keelson_get_request or keelson_get_purchase.

productUrl.description: The product page on the store.

observation.description: What the agent read on the store that led to this cart, verbatim. No personal data.

name: keelson_check_cart
description: Checks a cart against the mandate as it stands, without buying: whether a countersign would pass, and what to do about each blocker. Safe to call as often as needed.

name: keelson_request_countersign
description: Asks Keelson to countersign the cart under the mandate, with the evidence submitted for it. Keelson's two TEEs check every field; on allow, the purchase is logged, covered by the operator's bond and captured on PayPal. A block is Keelson's answer, not an error. Never call this tool again to finish or check what it started: that starts a new operation. Follow `next`, and poll keelson_get_request or keelson_get_purchase.

repeatOf.description: Only when the user explicitly asked to buy this same cart again: the purchase of it you got last. Never on a retry.

name: keelson_get_purchase
description: Reads a purchase: its state, amount, log index and capture. Safe to poll.

name: keelson_verify_alibi
description: Runs the verifier's checks on a purchase's Alibi: TEE signatures and attestations, log inclusion and cosignatures, timestamps and the on-chain anchor. The browser verifier is the reference.

name: keelson_export_alibi
description: The purchase in an agentic-commerce standard: AP2 mandates and receipts (ap2), a Mastercard Verifiable Intent chain (vi), a UCP checkout (ucp), an ACP allowance (acp), a signed Visa TAP request (tap) or the Visa evidence pack for a chargeback (visa). Each carries the purchase's SCITT transparent statement and is signed by Keelson's attested enclave.

name: keelson_get_trust_grade
description: An operator's trust grade (A to F), the premium each new coverage pays and the bond it should hold, from its coverages and verdicts.
